label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss) is TRUE POSITIVE. User-supplied cookie value flows directly to the XSS sink without effective neutralization. The sink expression 'Sensitive value \'' + org.owasp.esapi.ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(new String(input)) + "\'" writes encoded content to the browser. However, the critical flaw is that the sink concatenates the raw string representation ('Sensitive value \'' and '\'') around the encoded payload. While the payload itself is HTML-encoded, the surrounding quotes are not escaped for HTML context, allowing attackers to inject script tags within those literals (e.g., breaking out of the quote to inject '<script>alert(1)</script>'). The resolved sink value depends on user input and remains partially unescaped.

evidence.note: Sink writes user-derived input to HTML response. The string interpolation includes unescaped quotes around the encoded user value, enabling XSS.
